plain_english: Now this entire worship is taught through the glorious Kaula method, for the fit ones mounted on firm resolve of exactly that awakened kind. On this point the Yogasaṃcāra and the rest declare: bliss is Brahman, seated in the body, established threefold at lips and lowest end.
sanskrit_cite: atha samastā iyam upāsā samunmiṣattādṛśadṛḍhavāsanārūḍhān adhikāriṇaḥ prati śrīmatkaulikaprakriyayā nirūpyate tatra uktaṃ yogasaṃcārādau ānandaṃ brahma taddehe tridhauṣṭyāntyavyavasthitam

plain_english: Whoever abandons it, not abiding in Brahman, is cut off from bliss.
sanskrit_cite: abrahmacāriṇas tasya tyāgād ānandavarjitāḥ

plain_english: And sacrificers of the wheel who feed on blissless, artificial food —
sanskrit_cite: ānandakṛtrimāhāravarjaṃ cakrasya yājakāḥ

plain_english: both sink into dreadful hell. Therefore one should hold to this stance.
sanskrit_cite: dvaye 'pi narake ghore tasmād enāṃ sthitiṃ bhajet

plain_english: So in this stance there is the Kula sacrifice, and it is sixfold: in the outer, in the Śakti, in one’s own body, in the couple, in breath, and in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: tad anayā sthityā kulayāgaḥ sa ca ṣoḍhā bāhye śaktau svadehe yāmale prāṇe saṃvidi ca iti

plain_english: Here each later one is higher than the last, and each earlier one exists to give a taste for what follows.
sanskrit_cite: tatra ca uttara uttara utkṛṣṭaḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvas tadrucyartham

plain_english: For one who seeks powers, the second, the fourth, and the fifth are to be carried out in every way; for one who seeks release the sixth is chief — yet even he must perform the second and the rest on occasional rites as far as possible, and to complete the rite.
sanskrit_cite: siddhikāmasya dvitīyaturyapañcamāḥ sarvathā nirvartyāḥ ṣaṣṭhas tu mumukṣoḥ mukhyaḥ tasyāpi dvitīyādyā naimittike yathāsambhavam anuṣṭheyā eva vidhipūraṇārthaṃ ca

plain_english: Among these, the outer consists of the bliss-full altar, the hero’s cup, a red cloth — or else the liṅga and the rest as mentioned before.
sanskrit_cite: tatra bāhyaṃ sthaṇḍilam ānandapūrṇaṃ vīrapātram aruṇaḥ paṭaḥ pūrvoktam api vā liṅgādi

plain_english: There, with no need at all for bathing and the rest of the duties — purity being gained by resting in full bliss alone — one should first contemplate the oneness of breath, consciousness, and body, and then utter the mantra twenty-seven times over crown, face, heart, secret place, and body, in forward and reverse order, since consciousness itself has Paramaśiva’s form: the fullness of the universe’s course made complete in the Supreme Lord — in the lower, in the middle, and in the highest alike.
sanskrit_cite: tatra snānādikartavyānapekṣayaiva pūrṇānandaviśrāntyaiva labdhaśuddhiḥ prathamaṃ prāṇasaṃviddehaikībhāvaṃ bhāvayitvā saṃvidaś ca paramaśivarūpatvāt saptaviṃśativāraṃ mantram uccārya mūrdhavaktrahṛdguhyamūrtiṣu anulomavilomābhyāṃ viśvādhvaparipūrṇatā parameśvare aparatve parāparatve paratve 'pi ca

plain_english: For so it is: from Māyā, person, nature, and intellect beginning, down to earth, there are twenty-seven tattvas — kalā and the rest included therein — and likewise, in the knowledge-power in the middle state, the qualities of the Brahman-pentad, beginning with instant-ness, born-ness, and become-arisen-ness, number just twenty-seven in form. So declare the glorious Lakulīśa masters.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi māyāpuṃprakṛtiguṇadhīprabhṛti dharāntaṃ saptaviṃśatitattvāni kalādīnāṃ tatraiva antarbhāvāt vidyāśaktāv api parāparatve brahmapañcakasya sadyastvājātatvabhavodbhavatvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saptaviṃśatirūpatvam eva uktaṃ śrīmallakuleśādipādaiḥ

plain_english: In the highest too the Lord is five-powered: to each power belong five forms, making twenty-five powers. Mutually undivided, they are a single power, still undivided — hence by a pervasion twenty-seven-formed one should bind the buddhi-and-breath-formed flame of consciousness-fire with a single utterance alone, so that Paramaśiva alone stands bound and it hastens toward nothing beyond the tantra. Thus penetrated, one should render the present offering-substance, dwelling, directions, and supports made of that very stuff; then one should fill the offering vessel by the tuft-binding pervasion alone and worship it, worship the altars with its drops, and — joining the left ring-finger with the thumb — worship and satisfy the mantra-wheel upon the body’s wheels with its essence. Then, up to breath; then fashion the trident-formed seat ending in the three powers upon the altar — up to Māyā, in the lettered auṃ-syllable fashion the seat ending in the three powers — up to Māyā in the lettered auṃ-syllable; and thereupon the power to be worshipped, deliberation-formed. Thus, by a single utterance alone, having effected the placing of support and supported, one should behold the universe right there — even in the consciousness that has become the supported — and that too as made of consciousness. So the universe through consciousness, and through that, her mutual enclosure comes about: arisen from consciousness, it comes to rest right there — for the universe rises from the knowable, and consciousness rests right there. Just this much is the consciousness-principle, attained through the twofold enclosure.
sanskrit_cite: paratve 'pi pañcaśaktiḥ hi parameśvaraḥ pratiśakti ca pañcarūpatā evaṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ śaktayaḥ tāś ca anyonyam anudbhinnavibhāgā ity ekā śaktiḥ sā cānudbhinnavibhāgā ity evaṃ saptaviṃśatirūpayā vyāptyā saṃvidagneḥ śikhāṃ buddhiprāṇarūpāṃ sakṛduccāramātreṇaiva baddhāṃ kuryāt yena paramaśiva eva pratibaddhā tantrātiriktaṃ na kiṃcid abhidhāvati tathāvidhabuddhyadhiṣṭhitakaraṇacakrānuvedhena purovartino yāgadravyagṛhadigādhārādīn api tanmayībhūtān kuryāt tato 'rghapātram api śikhābandhavyāptyaiva pūrayet pūjayec ca tadvipruḍbhiḥ sthaṇḍilāny api tadrasena vāmānāmāṅguṣṭhayogāt dehacakreṣu mantracakraṃ pūjayet tarpayet ca tataḥ prāṇāntaḥ tataḥ sthaṇḍile triśūlātmakaṃ śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ kalpayet māyāntaṃ hi sārṇe aukāre ca śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ kalpayet māyāntaṃ hi sārṇe aukāre ca śaktitrayāntaṃ tadupari yājyā vimarśarūpā śaktiḥ ity evaṃ sakṛd uccāreṇaiva ādhārādheyanyāsaṃ kṛtvā tatraiva ādheyabhūtāyām api saṃvidi viśvaṃ paśyet tad api ca saṃvinmayam ity evaṃ viśvasya saṃvidā tena ca tasyāḥ saṃpuṭībhāvo bhavati saṃvida uditaṃ tatraiva paryavasitaṃ yato viśvaṃ vedyāc ca saṃvit udeti tatraiva ca viśrāmyati iti etāvattvaṃ saṃvittattvaṃ saṃpuṭībhāvadvayāt labhyate

plain_english: So it has been said: having fully enclosed emission.
sanskrit_cite: tad uktam sṛṣṭiṃ tu saṃpuṭīkṛtya iti

plain_english: Then, having offered incense, smoke, wine, flowers, and the rest, down to self-surrender, having murmured in one’s own rest and gathered it all in, one should cast it into water.
sanskrit_cite: tato gandhadhūpāsavakusumādīn ātmaprahvībhāvāntān arpayitvā svaviśrāntyā japtvā upasaṃhṛtya jale nikṣipet

plain_english: Thus concludes the outer sacrifice.
sanskrit_cite: iti bāhyayāgaḥ

plain_english: Now, in the Śakti. There — the goddesses and heroes of the Śakti-circle being mutually of both natures, from the awakening of Śiva and Śakti that runs from play's beginning to emission's end, through mutual activity, by the Supreme Lord's ordainment, in pure form — preeminence lies there. By this, even the distinguished wheel's Śakti-ness stands explained. There, worship is by the tuft-binding pervasion alone, upon the seat ending in the three powers; in the triangle, in the middle, the emission-power — but in the pervasion lies the distinction.
sanskrit_cite: atha śaktau tatra anyonyaṃ śaktitālāsāvīrāṇām ubhayeṣām ubhayātmakatvena prollāsaprārambhasṛṣṭyantaśivaśaktiprabodhe parasparaṃ vyāpārāt parameśaniyatyā ca śuddharūpatayā tatra prādhānyam etena ca viśiṣṭacakrasyāpi śaktitvaṃ vyākhyātam tatra śikhābandhavyāptyaiva pūjanaṃ śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ koṇatraye madhye visargaśaktiḥ iti tu vyāptau viśeṣaḥ

plain_english: So too in one's own body: in that very wheel there; then in the sub-wheels beginning with the crown-aperture.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ svadehe tatraiva cakre tato brahmarandhrādyanucakreṣu

plain_english: Now, in the couple. This is the mark of the Śakti: like that — non-difference. Then, disregarding age, birth, and the rest, out of non-attachment; for identity is born of the transgressive pair.
sanskrit_cite: atha yāmale śakter lakṣaṇam etat tadvad abhedas tato 'napekṣya vayaḥ jātyādīṃś cāsaṅgāt loketarayugalajaṃ hi tādātmyam

plain_english: From being arisen together with cause and effect, threefold — directly, or else in arranged fashion — the two, having worshipped one another, draw bliss near by satisfying.
sanskrit_cite: kāryahetusahotthatvāt traidhaṃ sākṣād athānyathā kḷptāvato mitho 'bhyarcya tarpyānandāntikatvataḥ

plain_english: One should worship the wheel according to its fitness, and likewise the sub-wheel that follows — outwardly with flowers and the rest, ending inward, and with perfumes, foods, wines, and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: cakram arcet tadaucityād anucakraṃ tathānugam bahiḥ puṣpādināntaś ca gandhabhuktyāsavādibhiḥ

plain_english: Such is the state surging with the play of that bliss-mass. And the host of sub-wheels dissolves through identity with the wheel.
sanskrit_cite: evam ānandasaṃdohitatacceṣṭocchalatsthitiḥ anucakragaṇaś cakratādātmyād abhilīyate

plain_english: In the relish of own-being at the time when each enjoyment unfolds, gradually the sub-wheel goddesses enter the middle consciousness-wheel.
sanskrit_cite: nijanijabhogābhogapravikāsamayasvarūpaparimarśe kramaśo 'nucakradevyaḥ saṃviccakraṃ hi madhyamaṃ yānti

plain_english: That whose power is won by filling the host of rays embodied in the sub-wheel goddesses — having the nature of that power, like that — becomes mutually facing.
sanskrit_cite: anucakradevatātmakamarīcigaṇapūraṇādhigatavīryam tacchaktitadvadātmakam anyonyasamunmukhaṃ bhavati

plain_english: The agitation born of the throbbing entry into the upper abode of that pair agitates the sub-wheels as well — and then they are made of that, not separate.
sanskrit_cite: tadyugalamūrdhvadhāmapraveśasaspandajātasaṃkṣobham kṣubhnāty anucakrāṇy api tāni tadā tanmayāni na pṛthak tu

plain_english: Such is this couple, whose talk of difference has melted away: just when it is so, then, through gradation and excellence, she indeed is the collision of consciousness and emission.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ yāmalam etad galitabhidāsaṃkathaṃ yadaiva tadā kramatāratamyayogāt saiva hi saṃvidvisargasaṃghaṭṭaḥ

plain_english: The steady supreme abode of that — the both-natured, vast world — bliss is neither the calm nor the arisen: the womb-cause of the calm and the arisen, the supreme Kaula.
sanskrit_cite: taddhruvadhāmānuttaram ubhayātmakajagad udāram ānandam no śāntaṃ nāpy uditaṃ śāntoditasūtikāraṇaṃ paraṃ kaulam

plain_english: Desiring the undivided station, one should make her — consciousness — one's own; then the pair, calm-natured and arisen-natured, rises at once for power and for power-bearer.
sanskrit_cite: anavacchinnapadepsus tāṃ saṃvidam ātmasātkuryāt śāntoditātmakadvayam atha yugapad udeti śaktiśaktimatoḥ

plain_english: From the interpenetration of self and other, when there is calm and other — of the two, through two-naturedness — power, though arisen like that, nourishes emission; its bearer does not.
sanskrit_cite: svātmānyonyāveśāt śāntānyatve dvayor dvayātmatvāt śaktis tu tadvad uditāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ puṣṇāti no tadvān

plain_english: In her lies the excellent Kula. Then, through her, among men, come the taught collisions of yoga. Then — in the twofold emission, in this calm-arisen abode — those who contemplate —
sanskrit_cite: tasyāṃ cāryaṃ kulam atha tayā nṛṣu proktayogasaṃghaṭṭān atha sṛṣṭe dvitaye 'smin śāntoditadhāmni ye 'nusaṃdadhate

plain_english: In the eastward one, mounted in the undivided station as emission-being — the arisen, too, is received mutually from mouth to mouth, from the chief mouth outward into the mouth.
sanskrit_cite: prācyāṃ visargasattām anavacchidite pade rūḍhāḥ uditaṃ ca mitho vaktrān mukhyād vaktre pragṛhyate ca bahiḥ

plain_english: The goddess-wheel becomes satisfied, bestowing powers, knowledge, and release. In the practice of calm, one attains the calm Śiva — which here is the wheel of deities.
sanskrit_cite: tṛptaṃ devīcakraṃ siddhijñānāpavargadaṃ bhavati śāntābhyāse śāntaṃ śivam eti yad atra devatācakram

plain_english: The void, devoid of bliss — from bliss's own abode the offering — and the humming-thrilled ones, through the taste of relishing outward states filled with one's own essence.
sanskrit_cite: śūnyaṃ nirānandamayaṃ nirvṛtinijadhāmato 'rghaṃ ca raṇaraṇakarasān nijarasabharitabahirbhāvacarvaṇarasena

plain_english: The sub-wheel surging with inner fullness reaches the wheel; then that too surges as before. Thus this emission is threefold in its implied sense.
sanskrit_cite: āntarapūrṇasamucchaladanucakraṃ yāti cakram atha tad api ucchalati prāgvad iti trividho 'nvartho visargo 'yam

plain_english: In this emission-abode, through relish, mantra-power — in just three ways — bears each fruit in each consciousness-womb.
sanskrit_cite: etad visargadhāmani parimarśanatas tridhaiva manuvīryam tattatsaṃvidgarbhe mantras tattatphalaṃ sūte

plain_english: Upon the lotus that covers eternal, rising auspiciousness, resting within the triangle — the stalk never parted, rooted in the true sixteen-petalled lotus.
sanskrit_cite: koṇatrayāntarāśritanityoditamaṅgalacchade kamale nityāviyutaṃ nālaṃ ṣoḍaśadalakamalasanmūlam

plain_english: In the fire at the course of rubbing the pair of lotuses strung upon the central stalk — from the collision, in the middle, of moon-beauty and the flood of the sun's rays.
sanskrit_cite: madhyasthanālagumphitasarojayugaghaṭṭanakramādagnau madhyasthaśaśadharasundaradinakarakaraughasaṃghaṭṭāt

plain_english: From union with the three-petalled ruddy ray of power, in the middle — sprout-emission. Thus, by the seal of the wondrous gathering of moon and sun, in a flash.
sanskrit_cite: tridalāruṇavīryakalāsaṅgān madhye 'ṅkurasṛṣṭiḥ iti śaśadharavāsarapaticitraguṣaṃghaṭṭamudrayā jhaṭiti

plain_english: Carrying out within the order that begins with emission, one gains steadiness in the fourth — this in the entry of the sky-going seal, mutually, of one's own power and power-bearer.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭyādikramam antaḥ kurvaṃs turye sthitiṃ labhate etat khecaramudrāveśe 'nyonyaṃ svaśaktiśaktimatoḥ

plain_english: Whoever would abide made of relish amid drinking, enjoyment, play, laughter, and the rest — with unmanifest sound, roar, outburst, hearing, tone, and tone's end.
sanskrit_cite: pānopabhogalīlāhāsādiṣu yo bhaved vimarśamayaḥ avyaktadhvanirāvasphoṭaśrutinādanādāntaiḥ

plain_english: That mantra-power, with unbroken, unstruck ultimate realities — in the rests of going and coming, in the ear, in the eye, in contact with the double mark.
sanskrit_cite: avyucchinnānāhataparamārthair mantravīryaṃ tat gamanāgamaviśrāntiṣu karṇe nayane dvilakṣyasamparke

plain_english: In the yoga of their closing, called the body's end — and in the couple, in the wheel — that which, throat-reaching from the heart-place between the breasts to the lip's end, is unmanifest.
sanskrit_cite: tatsammīlanayoge dehāntākhye ca yāmale cakre kucamadhyahṛdayadeśād oṣṭhānte kaṇṭhagaṃ yad avyaktam

plain_english: Having heard that which lies between the two wheels, when agitation ends they come to rest there — and thus this is the supreme eightfold Nāda-Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite: tac cakradvayamadhyagam ākarṇya kṣobhavigamasamaye yat nirvānti tatra caivaṃ yo 'ṣṭavidho nādabhairavaḥ paramaḥ

plain_english: Since she is light and sound, that mantra-bearing pervasion is called the highest: in every act, for the knower, there would be release while living.
sanskrit_cite: jyotir dhvaniś ca yasmāt sā māntrī vyāptir ucyate paramā karmaṇi karmaṇi viduṣaḥ syāj jīvato muktiḥ

plain_english: Knowing that, liberated in scripture — a vessel of alien Kula wisdom is the womb — one should make the void-and-nonvoid abode, with fire and wind in the single staff.
sanskrit_cite: tajjñaḥ śāstre muktaḥ parakulavijñānabhājanaṃ garbhaḥ śūnyāśūnyālayaṃ kuryād ekadaṇḍe 'nalānilau

plain_english: Having made the trident of one taste — essence abiding in essence, as it were — with doubt abandoned, riteless: I am not — thus contemplating.
sanskrit_cite: śūlaṃ samarasīkṛtya rase rasam iva sthitam tyaktāśaṅko nirācāro nāham asmīti bhāvayan

plain_english: Beholding the goddesses dwelling in the body — joy, agitation, and the rest in the mass of consciousness — the host of goddesses stationed in the wheels of ear, eye, mouth, and nose.
sanskrit_cite: dehasthā devatāḥ paśyan hlādodvegādi ciddhane karṇākṣimukhanāsādicakrasthaṃ devatāgaṇam

plain_english: Ever beholding the grasper — by Khecarī one succeeds, certainly.
sanskrit_cite: grahītāraṃ sadā paśyan khecaryā sidhyati dhruvam

plain_english: In a far distant chasm, in a flash hurling one's own body — dwelling without violence, having drawn in both hands, gazing — one should practice this sky-going seal.
sanskrit_cite: śvabhre sudūre jhaṭiti svadehaṃ saṃpātayan vāsam asāhasena ākuñcya hastadvitayaṃ prapaśyan mudrām imāṃ vyomacarīṃ bhajeta

plain_english: Thus this is the sacrifice of the couple.
sanskrit_cite: ity eṣa yāmalayāgaḥ

plain_english: In the stated-pervaded breath, made of the universe — strengthening, by the taught pervasion of consciousness, through the offering of libation, food, perfume, incense, and the rest — that is breath-sacrifice.
sanskrit_cite: uktavyāptike prāṇe viśvamaye proktasaṃvidvyāptyā tarpaṇānnagandhadhūpādisamarpaṇena upodbalanaṃ prāṇayāgaḥ

plain_english: But rest's establishment is consciousness-sacrifice — already taught before.
sanskrit_cite: viśrāntirūḍhis tu saṃvidyāgaḥ prāg eva nirūpitaḥ

plain_english: Thus, having performed any one of these sacrifices — should the disciple become one whose heart is painted with such doubtlessness — then for him, preceded by the beholding of that sacrifice and needing no prior offering of sesame and ghee, one should perform initiation by a glance, in the order of contemplation through the aforesaid pervasion. But at the close of the occasional rite, for indirect initiation and the rest, the earlier rule alone holds.
sanskrit_cite: evam etebhyo yāgebhyo 'nyatamaṃ kṛtvā yadi tathāvidhanirvicikitsatāpacitritahṛdayaḥ śiṣyo bhavati tadā tasmai tadyāgadarśanapūrvakaṃ tilājyāhutipūrvakanirapekṣam eva pūrvoktavyāptyā anusaṃdhānakrameṇa avalokanayā dīkṣāṃ kuryāt parokṣadīkṣādike naimittikānte tu pūrva eva vidhiḥ

plain_english: Merely by the primacy of sacrifice is this so.
sanskrit_cite: kevalam etad yāgapradhānatayā iti

plain_english: In the guru's body lies the seventh Kula sacrifice, most excellent of all — and it too, performed but once before in the company of the sacrifices, fulfills everything. Śivam.
sanskrit_cite: guruśarīre saptamaḥ kulayāgaḥ sarvottamaḥ so 'pi prāg yāgasāhityena sakṛd eva kṛtaḥ sarvaṃ pūrayati iti śivam
